profile.address: 5420 Tulane Road, Memphis, Shelby County, TN 38109
profile.reading:
This is xAI's Colossus 2 building in the Scaife area of southwest Memphis, Tennessee, a large single structure on Tulane Road tagged in mapping data at 5420 Tulane Road and identified in federal court filings by the campus address 5400 Tulane Road. It stands just north of the Tennessee and Mississippi state line, and that detail is the single most important fact about the site, because the building's load is in Shelby County while the plant that feeds it is in DeSoto County, Mississippi. xAI announced the second Memphis data center in early March 2025 and began installing computing infrastructure at this site in July 2025. On March 3, 2026 the company filed a construction permit with the Memphis and Shelby County Division of Planning and Development valued at about 659.3 million dollars for a four story, 75 foot building expanding the Colossus 2 site on adjoining ground.

On power the record has to be read carefully, because four different quantities get reported as though they were one. No operator statement or filing reviewed for this page gives an IT load for this building, so none is recorded. Nor is there an established utility service level. In a public update dated May 5, 2025, Memphis Light, Gas and Water said that for the Tulane Road site no final power request had been submitted, that it was not then conducting a system impact study for the site, and that early discussions had ranged anywhere from 260 megawatts to 1.1 gigawatts. That range is a description of conversations, not a service commitment, and it should not be read as capacity. By contrast the utility described the separate Colossus 1 site on Paul R. Lowry Road in firm terms, 8 megawatts from an existing MLGW substation and 142 megawatts from a newly built one, with a further 150 megawatts sought from TVA toward a 300 megawatt target.

What actually powers Colossus 2 sits across the state line. A February 13, 2026 notice of intent to sue filed on behalf of the NAACP identified xAI's plant at 2875 Stanton Road in Southaven, Mississippi, owned by the xAI affiliate MZX Tech LLC, as the source serving Colossus II at 5400 Tulane Road, and counted 27 gas turbines there with a combined rating of at least 495 megawatts as of February 9, 2026. That is on site generation, not compute capacity, and it belongs to the Southaven parcel rather than to this building. xAI's own July 30, 2026 statement describes a 1.2 gigawatt plant under construction with 41 permanent turbines, with temporary mobile units to be removed by July 2027.

The Memphis air permit fight that drew national attention concerned the other campus, not this one. The Shelby County Health Department issued permit 01156-01PC-070225 on July 2, 2025 authorizing 15 turbines at Colossus 1 after receiving more than 1,700 public comments. The NAACP Memphis branch and Young, Gifted and Green, represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center, appealed on July 16, 2025, arguing the turbines had been treated as exempt nonroad engines and that the site should have been permitted as an existing major source. The Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board dismissed that appeal on December 15, 2025 on mootness grounds. No comparable Shelby County air permit for turbines at this Tulane Road building appears in the record reviewed here, which is consistent with the generation having been sited in Mississippi.

profile.capacity_note: Keep the four quantities apart for this site. it_capacity_mw is absent, because no xAI statement, permit or filing reviewed here states an IT load for the Tulane Road building. utility_power_mw is also absent. The 260 megawatt to 1.1 gigawatt span that Memphis Light, Gas and Water reported on May 5, 2025 describes the range of early discussions for the site before any formal request or system impact study, so it is neither a contracted service size nor a capacity figure. The 495 megawatt and 1.2 gigawatt numbers that appear in filings and in xAI's own statements are on site generation at the separate Southaven, Mississippi plant, which is generation rather than load and sits on a different parcel in a different state. No standby diesel rating is established for this building.
profile.community_note: Public objection to xAI in Memphis has been sustained and organized. The Shelby County Health Department logged more than 1,700 public comments on the Colossus 1 turbine permit and a April 25, 2025 hearing drew hundreds of opponents. The NAACP Memphis branch, Young, Gifted and Green and the Southern Environmental Law Center have pressed the case through county appeal and then federal court, arguing that turbine emissions fall on South Memphis neighborhoods that already carry elevated asthma and cancer risk. xAI and the Greater Memphis Chamber have pointed to jobs, investment, emissions control equipment and a recycled wastewater plant built by the company. Residents near the Tulane Road site have also raised construction noise and traffic with local officials.
profile.regulatory_note: Air permitting for the generation that serves this building falls to Mississippi rather than to Shelby County, because the turbines are sited south of the state line. The Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board granted a permit for 41 turbines at the Southaven plant on March 10, 2026, that decision was appealed by the Southern Environmental Law Center on April 9, 2026, and a Clean Air Act suit over the previously unpermitted temporary turbines is pending in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi. On the Tennessee side, the Shelby County Health Department air permit issued July 2, 2025 and the Air Pollution Control Board appeal dismissed December 15, 2025 both concern Colossus 1 on Paul R. Lowry Road, not this building.
profile.campus_power_note: The Memphis campus is split across three sites and two states. Colossus 1 on Paul R. Lowry Road takes grid power from Memphis Light, Gas and Water and TVA, reported by the utility in May 2025 as 8 megawatts from an existing substation plus 142 megawatts from a new one, with a further 150 megawatts sought toward a 300 megawatt target, and it holds a Shelby County Health Department air permit for 15 gas turbines. This Tulane Road building had no final MLGW power request as of that update. Its electricity comes principally from xAI's own gas turbine plant at 2875 Stanton Road in Southaven, Mississippi, held by the affiliate MZX Tech LLC, which the company describes as a 1.2 gigawatt plant under construction with 41 permanent turbines. That generation is tracked on the Southaven entry in this registry and is not attributed to this building.

reading.body:
xAI Colossus 2 is a 1-million-square-foot expansion building acquired in March 2025 at 5400 Tulane Road in Memphis's Whitehaven neighborhood, designed to house approximately 110,000 GB200 GPUs as part of xAI's stated goal of expanding the Colossus campus to 1 million GPUs total. No building-specific power capacity or opening date has been published; the campus-level figure of up to 250 MW at Colossus 1 and expansion plans toward nearly 2 GW across a third building are operator statements but not confirmed for this building alone. The facility is part of a campus whose Colossus 1 site required 35 gas turbines totaling 422 MW combined output and Tesla Megapack battery storage after its original 150 MW grid connection proved insufficient for GPU-cluster demand, drawing environmental scrutiny over nitrogen oxide emissions and water usage.

Colossus 2 sits in Tennessee at a state where only 4 of 24 mapped data center facilities have published power figures, and those 4 total 12.13 MW. This campus, if the 110,000 additional GB200 units draw power at typical AI training density, would require assumptions about per-unit power consumption not yet published in building-specific terms. The operator's stated expansion to independent power supply independent from Memphis utilities signals that grid constraints have already shaped buildout decisions at Colossus 1 and inform infrastructure planning for Colossus 2.

The binding constraint on this campus's scaling is power availability and grid interconnection capacity in the Memphis region, where municipal peak demand sits around 3 GW total. No building-specific certifications, security accreditations, or tenant restrictions have been published for Colossus 2. The site matters to AI scaling primarily as a deployed expansion of an existing 1-million-GPU campus strategy by a major compute operator, but without facility-level power and operational milestones, its actual contribution to AI capacity remains unquantified.
